quiz.question: Why does count zero return before pointer use?

choices.text: An empty computation has no input or output memory accesses.
Every pointer is then automatically aligned.
A zero word always means a black frame.

hints.text: Treat the count as unsigned before calculating a byte extent.
Only a positive count requires usable word-aligned windows.

choices.text: The complete XOR word is nonzero.
The XOR word is positive as a signed number.

hints.text: A Boolean zero/nonzero result contributes at most one per word.
Keep the word count separate from the four-byte pointer increments.

quiz.question: How many native words are in one admitted vector group?

hints.text: Each vector contains sixteen bytes and each word uses four.
Test the word remainder, not whether at least one word remains.

quiz.question: Why must both vector inputs be loaded before the store?

choices.text: Output may exactly alias an input.
The CRC needs the output first.

hints.text: The operation is bitwise across the vector, while its memory representation is word-oriented.
Retain the result vector for the next lane-count step.

quiz.question: How many changes does a group with two nonzero word lanes contribute?

choices.text: The number of nonzero bytes in those lanes.

hints.text: A word with only bit 31 set is still a nonzero word.
Contribute one Boolean for each of the four word lanes.

quiz.question: After a four-word group, how far does each pointer advance?

hints.text: Advance each pointer by sixteen bytes and reduce words remaining by four.
The supplied empty-tail test prevents a load after an exact group boundary.
